$comment: TIER 1 — primitive reference tones. ADR-007 decision 2: primitives are
BUILD-TIME ONLY. No --_tekad-ref-* custom property is ever emitted; the
generator resolves these to sRGB and only the semantic tier reaches the
stylesheet. That is what keeps :root small — a variant axis must never
become a selector, and a primitive ramp must never become a payload.
Tones are authored in OKLCH because it is perceptually uniform, so an even
lightness ramp looks even. It says NOTHING about WCAG contrast — see
tools/lib/color.mjs and ADR-007 decision 6. Contrast is asserted separately,
Tone numbers are OKLCH lightness x 100, so tone 40 is L=0.40. Higher is
lighter, in both schemes — the ramp does not invert for dark mode; the

neutral.$comment: Near-achromatic with a trace of the brand hue, so greys sit with the palette instead of beside it.

brand.$comment: A blue-violet. Chroma is held below the sRGB gamut edge across the whole ramp so no tone is silently clamped.

$comment: Chroma is reduced at the extremes of the ramp. Full chroma at tone 98 or
tone 10 leaves the sRGB gamut, and an out-of-gamut colour renders at a
different contrast than the one that was computed — which would make the
contrast gate assert something the browser does not display.
